target.what: Worldwide installed AI-accelerator compute capacity expressed in H100-equivalents (i.e., aggregate accelerator throughput normalized to one NVIDIA H100 GPU, using a stated precision convention such as dense FP16/BF16 or FP8), counting both training and inference/deployment use, as a stock at the cut
target.publisher: No official publisher; analyst synthesis from vendor shipment data, cloud capex disclosures, and third-party accelerator trackers
target.caveats: Ambiguous and unmeasured quantity. Working interpretation: total worldwide installed base of AI accelerators (NVIDIA datacenter GPUs, AMD Instinct, Google TPU, AWS Trainium/Inferentia, custom ASICs, and Chinese accelerators such as Huawei Ascend) converted to H100-equivalents via a stated precision

candidates.hypothesis: NVIDIA datacenter GPU revenue and unit shipments (H100, H200, GH200/GB200, plus A100 legacy) form the largest single component of the H100-equivalent stock; cumulative shipments since 2022 approximate the NVIDIA share of installed capacity. Higher datacenter revenue implies proportionally more H100-equivalents.

assessment.note: All three report the same ~4 million Hopper GPUs delivered over 2023–Oct 2025; p1/p2 are the same moomoo keynote article, p77 is a Chinese-language retelling of the same NVIDIA keynote, so they are one underlying measurement, not three.

Same NVIDIA keynote: 20M Blackwell/Rubin chips 2025–26 = 10M Hopper-equivalents (dual-die), 6M shipped to date = 3M H100e, $500B revenue. Internally consistent but a single source and partly forward-looking.
One KGI report (June 2024) — all share a single model and vintage; 2025 figures are forecasts made before Blackwell ramp and are now stale.

One Epoch AI dataset reported through Network World: US hyperscalers >60% of global AI compute, Google ~25% (~5M H100e, 4M TPU), Microsoft 3.5M, Amazon 2.5M, Meta 2.25M, Oracle 1M. These are shares of the same total, so they are not independent of each other.

Epoch-derived figures via CryptoBriefing: 27.6M H100e sold by June 2026, 46M stock end-2026, 13.9M H100e in 86 tracked facilities = 44–46% of global. The 13.9M/0.45 ≈ 31M is consistent with the 27.6M sold figure plus deployment lag.

a1.role: Share of cumulative sold H100e still installed and operational at Oct 2026

methods.rationale: Direct Epoch-anchored route: 27.6M H100e sold by June 2026, rolled forward four months and discounted for retirement/idle. Shared dependency: p161 is Epoch's sales model, so this route inherits its definitional uncertainty (peak 8-bit ops). Failure mode: if Epoch's 27.6M is already an installed-stock figure rather than sales, a1 double-discounts.

p165.role: H100e GPUs housed in Epoch-tracked AI facilities as of September 2026

a3.role: Share of global AI compute held by Epoch-tracked facilities

methods.rationale: Bottom-up from tracked facilities: 13.9M H100e in 86 sites scaled by the inverse of Epoch's own 44–46% coverage estimate. Independent of the sales-model route in that it counts deployed capacity at named sites, though it shares Epoch as the underlying source. Failure mode: tracked facilities may be biased toward US hyperscalers, undercounting China and enterprise.

p224.role: Cumulative NVIDIA datacenter GPU units sold 2021–2024

a5.role: Average H100e per NVIDIA datacenter GPU shipped 2021–2026

a4.role: Non-NVIDIA share of global H100e stock

methods.rationale: Vendor-shipment route: 15.5M NVIDIA datacenter GPUs 2021–2024 (p224), converted to H100e via a mix-weighted factor, grossed up for non-NVIDIA share. This route omits 2025–2026 NVIDIA shipments (which p3/p76 suggest are large), so it is a lower-bound-flavored estimate; it is kept because it uses a genuinely different measurement (unit shipments) from the Epoch sales model. methods.rationale: Direct anchor: the only published end-2026 stock forecast (46M H100e). It is a forecast, not an observation, and is two months after the cutoff, so it is used as a cross-check rather than a primary estimate. Shared dependency with m1 (both Epoch-derived). assumptions.name: Share of cumulative H100e sold still installed and operational at Oct 2026
assumptions.rationale: Epoch's 27.6M is cumulative sold by June 2026; some A100/H100 units are retired or idle. p214 suggests a ~4M deployment lag on 20M sold (~80% deployed). Using 0.85 with a wide band reflects retirement of 2020–2022 A100s offset by rapid new deployment.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to cumulative H100e sold to convert sales to installed stock.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that retirement is negligible (stock ≈ sales) or that >30% of sold capacity is idle/stranded.

assumptions.name: H100e added between June 2026 and October 2026 as a fraction of the June cumulative
assumptions.rationale: Epoch's 3.3x/yr growth (p196) implies ~4 months adds ~45%, but that is a sales growth rate and the stock grows more slowly; the 46M end-2026 forecast (p162) vs 27.6M June implies ~67% in six months, so four months at ~18% is conservative and consistent with the lower end.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to roll the June 2026 cumulative forward to the 2026-10-24 cutoff.
assumptions.falsified_by: A direct October 2026 stock estimate materially below 30M or above 40M.

assumptions.name: Share of global AI compute held by Epoch-tracked facilities (inverse of p167)
assumptions.rationale: p167 states tracked facilities are 44–46% of global AI compute; the complement (untracked hyperscale, enterprise, China) is the remainder. Used to scale p165 up to a global total.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to p165 (13.9M H100e in tracked facilities, Sept 2026).
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that tracked facilities cover a materially different share (e.g., >60% or <35%).

assumptions.name: Non-NVIDIA share of global H100e stock
assumptions.rationale: Epoch p202 says NVIDIA >60% of compute; TrendForce p257 says ~70% of AI chip market. Using 65% NVIDIA implies 35% non-NVIDIA (Google TPU, AWS Trainium, AMD, Huawei, Cambricon).
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to NVIDIA cumulative H100e to gross up to global total.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that NVIDIA share is >80% or <50% of H100e compute.

assumptions.name: Average H100e per NVIDIA datacenter GPU shipped 2021–2026
assumptions.rationale: Hopper ≈ 1 H100e; Blackwell/Rubin dual-die ≈ 2 H100e per chip (p4/p7); A100 ≈ 0.4 H100e. With a mix shifting from A100/Hopper to Blackwell, the weighted average is above 1.0; 1.3 with a wide band.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to cumulative NVIDIA datacenter GPU units (p224 plus 2025–2026 additions).
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Blackwell is not ~2x H100 per chip or that A100 dominates the installed base.

assessment.note: All are Epoch AI shipment-based cumulative H100e series through mid/late 2026: p161 ~27.6M (June), p274 ~31.2M (Q2), p294 20.3M end-2025 extrapolated to p295 31.6M by Sept 2026. Same underlying measurement family (Epoch chip-sales tracker), so agreement is not independent confirmation; they are consistent vintages of one series and should be treated as one route.

Epoch facility-atlas coverage: p165 13.9M H100e in tracked sites (Sept), p275 14.4M (Oct 7), with coverage ~43-46% (p167, p276, p289). Same source and same coverage concept; the implied global total (~30-32M) is consistent with the shipment series. Not independent of p161/p274.

p173 and p211 are duplicate statements of the same Epoch figure (~15M H100e cumulative, >10 GW chip TDP) from the same January 2026 page; p174/p212 likewise duplicate. Redundant copies, one underlying measurement.

Apparent conflict (15M in Jan 2026 vs 27.6M in June 2026) is a period difference, not a contradiction: it implies roughly 1.8x growth in five months, consistent with the ~3.3-3.4x/yr growth rate (p196, p279) and the 2.5x four-quarter multiple (p280).
Forward path: 31.6M (Sept 2026) to 46M (end-2026) to 140M (end-2028) implies continued rapid growth; internally consistent with the growth-rate evidence but all from the same Epoch-derived analysis.

Epoch AI firm-level H100e capacity estimates: Google 5M (4M TPU), Microsoft 3.5M, Amazon 2.5M, Meta 2.25M, Oracle 1M; US hyperscalers >60% of global, Google ~25%. These sum to ~14.25M for the top five, consistent with the ~13.9-14.4M tracked-facility totals (p165, p275) and with the ~44% coverage claim. Same source family.

Supplier shares in H100e: Nvidia 63%, Google 25%, Amazon 5%, AMD 4%, Huawei 3%, Cambricon <1% (Q2 2026); p202 (>60% Nvidia) and p257 (~70% Nvidia market share 2025) are consistent with a slowly declining Nvidia share. p257 is a revenue/market-share measure, not H100e, so it is corroborative context only.

Hopper lifecycle: 4M GPUs / $100B revenue (p1, p2, p77) and 3M Hopper-equivalents already shipped of 6M Blackwell/Rubin units (p7). p7's 'Hopper-equivalent' conversion of Blackwell units is a different normalization than raw unit counts and should not be mixed with p1/p77 unit counts.

NVIDIA unit counts differ by source and vintage: p220-p224 (7.52M in 2024, 15.5M cumulative 2021-24) are far above p13 (4.0M 2024F) and p14 (4.7-4.8M 2025F) and p76 (6M in 2025). The trustinsights figures appear to count all datacenter GPUs including legacy/low-end and may be inflated; KGI is a 2024 forecast. These are not interchangeable and should not be medianed together.

TPU shipments 0.5M/2.4M/1.75M (2023-25) and 3M forecast 2026 (p72-p75) vs Trainium >1M deployed (p65) and Trainium2 >2M shipped 2024-25 (p210). Different vendors, so independent; both indicate non-NVIDIA custom silicon is a material but minority share, consistent with p305/p306.

TPUv7 ~2.3x H100 (p148/p261) is consistent with the Google-published FP8 peak of 4614 TFLOP for TPU7x vs H100's ~1979 TFLOP (p316 vs p327): ratio ~2.33. This validates the H100e conversion convention for TPUv7; other chip ratios remain unsourced.
Trainium2 1.3 PFLOPS FP8 vs H100 1.98 PFLOPS FP8 gives ~0.66 H100e per Trainium2; Trainium3 5.2 PFLOPS gives ~2.6 H100e. These are the per-chip ratios needed to convert p65/p210 into H100e.

AI datacenter power estimates span 8 GW (p80/p84, 2025), 13.3 GW (p166, tracked facilities only), 29.6 GW (p176, 2025), 30 GW (p92, 2026) and >10 GW chip TDP (p174). These differ in scope (AI-dedicated vs tracked vs total AI-related) and in whether they are chip TDP or facility power; they cannot be reconciled into one power route without a stated kW/H100e and a consistent boundary.

Hardware power specs agree across sources: H100 700W TDP, 8-GPU node ~10.2 kW, B200 1000-1200W, GB200 NVL72 120-140 kW for 72 GPUs. These support a power-to-H100e conversion but the conversion also needs a fleet-mix and utilization assumption.

assumptions.name: Share of cumulative H100e sold still installed and operational at Oct 2026
assumptions.rationale: Cumulative sales overstate the installed stock because of retirement, resale, and the lag between delivery and deployment (p298 assumes a 3-month deployment delay). Most H100e sold since 2022 are still in service; a modest haircut is appropriate.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to a cumulative-sales figure to convert it to an installed stock at the cutoff.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence of large-scale retirement or resale of Hopper-class GPUs, or a documented sold-vs-deployed gap much larger than ~15%.

assumptions.name: H100e added between June 2026 and October 2026 as a fraction of the June cumulative
assumptions.rationale: Growth of ~3.3-3.4x/yr (p196, p279) implies ~11% per month, so four months would add ~50%; but the 2.5x four-quarter multiple (p280) and the 20.3M-to-31.6M path (p294, p295) suggest slower recent growth. A range of 8-30% brackets the plausible four-month increment.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to roll a June 2026 cumulative figure forward to October 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published monthly H100e shipment series showing a four-month increment outside 8-30%.

assumptions.name: Share of global AI compute held by Epoch-tracked facilities
assumptions.rationale: Epoch's own coverage estimates are 43-46% (p167, p276, p289), with a wide 90% interval of 23-81% (p277, p278). The central value is taken from the published point estimates; the range is narrowed toward the point estimates rather than the full 23-81% interval.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to scale tracked-facility H100e up to the global total.
assumptions.falsified_by: A revised Epoch coverage estimate outside 40-55%.

assumptions.name: Non-NVIDIA share of global H100e stock
assumptions.rationale: Epoch Q2 2026 supply shares: Nvidia 63%, Google 25%, Amazon 5%, AMD 4%, Huawei 3%, Cambricon <1% (p304-p309). The non-NVIDIA share is ~37% of supply; the installed stock may differ slightly because Nvidia's share has been declining, so a range of 25-45% is used.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to gross up an NVIDIA-only stock to the global total.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that Nvidia's installed-base share is materially above 75% or below 55%.

assumptions.name: Average H100e per NVIDIA datacenter GPU shipped 2021-2026
assumptions.rationale: The fleet mixes A100 (~0.3 H100e), H100/H200 (~1.0), and Blackwell (~2-3 H100e). With Hopper and Blackwell dominating recent shipments, the shipment-weighted average is above 1.0; a range of 1.0-1.8 reflects the mix uncertainty.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert NVIDIA datacenter GPU unit counts to H100e.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published per-architecture H100e conversion table showing a materially different average.

methods.label: m1

p161.role: Cumulative H100e chips sold worldwide as of June 2026

a2.role: Fractional H100e added June-Oct 2026 relative to June cumulative

a1.role: Share of cumulative sold H100e still installed and operational at Oct 2026

methods.rationale: Shipment-based route: Epoch's cumulative H100e sold through June 2026 (p161), rolled forward four months by a2 and haircut for retirement by a1. Shared dependency: p161 is the same Epoch series as p274/p294/p295, so this route is not independent of m2. Failure mode: if Epoch's cumulative figure is a sales rather than installed-stock measure, a1 must absorb the gap.

methods.label: m2

p165.role: H100e GPUs housed in Epoch-tracked AI facilities as of September 2026

a3.role: Share of global AI compute held by Epoch-tracked facilities

methods.rationale: Facility-atlas route: tracked-facility H100e (p165) divided by Epoch's own coverage share (a3). Shared dependency: p165 and a3 both come from Epoch's atlas, so the coverage estimate is not independent of the numerator. Failure mode: if coverage is understated, the global total is overstated.

weight_basis.m1: B1 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks
weight_basis.m2: B2 of 2 blocks; geometric mean of blocks

combination.weight_gate: off: inverse backtest-error weights need a bank-level gate (>= 30 scored questions with >= 2 backtested routes, hit rate >= 0.7; METHODS_ZH 4.1), which has not been run

interval.rule: several blocks: root mean square of the block widths, times the Birge ratio when it exceeds 1

kept.name: Share of cumulative H100e sold still installed and operational at Oct 2026
kept.rationale: Cumulative sales overstate the installed stock because of retirement, resale, and the lag between delivery and deployment (p298 assumes a 3-month deployment delay). Most H100e sold since 2022 are still in service; a modest haircut is appropriate.
kept.applies_when: Applied to a cumulative-sales figure to convert it to an installed stock at the cutoff.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence of large-scale retirement or resale of Hopper-class GPUs, or a documented sold-vs-deployed gap much larger than ~15%.

kept.name: H100e added between June 2026 and October 2026 as a fraction of the June cumulative
kept.rationale: Growth of ~3.3-3.4x/yr (p196, p279) implies ~11% per month, so four months would add ~50%; but the 2.5x four-quarter multiple (p280) and the 20.3M-to-31.6M path (p294, p295) suggest slower recent growth. A range of 8-30% brackets the plausible four-month increment.
kept.applies_when: Used to roll a June 2026 cumulative figure forward to October 2026.
kept.falsified_by: A published monthly H100e shipment series showing a four-month increment outside 8-30%.

kept.name: Share of global AI compute held by Epoch-tracked facilities
kept.rationale: Epoch's own coverage estimates are 43-46% (p167, p276, p289), with a wide 90% interval of 23-81% (p277, p278). The central value is taken from the published point estimates; the range is narrowed toward the point estimates rather than the full 23-81% interval.
kept.applies_when: Used to scale tracked-facility H100e up to the global total.
kept.falsified_by: A revised Epoch coverage estimate outside 40-55%.

kept.name: Non-NVIDIA share of global H100e stock
kept.rationale: Epoch Q2 2026 supply shares: Nvidia 63%, Google 25%, Amazon 5%, AMD 4%, Huawei 3%, Cambricon <1% (p304-p309). The non-NVIDIA share is ~37% of supply; the installed stock may differ slightly because Nvidia's share has been declining, so a range of 25-45% is used.
kept.applies_when: Used to gross up an NVIDIA-only stock to the global total.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that Nvidia's installed-base share is materially above 75% or below 55%.

kept.name: Average H100e per NVIDIA datacenter GPU shipped 2021-2026
kept.rationale: The fleet mixes A100 (~0.3 H100e), H100/H200 (~1.0), and Blackwell (~2-3 H100e). With Hopper and Blackwell dominating recent shipments, the shipment-weighted average is above 1.0; a range of 1.0-1.8 reflects the mix uncertainty.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert NVIDIA datacenter GPU unit counts to H100e.
kept.falsified_by: A published per-architecture H100e conversion table showing a materially different average.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
